test_inventory.coverage_conclusion: No active test directly toggles eager_mode, names defeq_fail_cache/congr_fail_cache, or asserts mode-separated negative-cache entries. Existing declaration traversal can incidentally call def_eq, but there is no demonstrated mode-differentiating same-context regression. findings.finding: The negative cache uses ordered (x,y,eager_mode) keys. It is consulted after def_eq_quick_check and records only false results that reach the final result block; early false quick checks need not populate it.

Eager mode does not allow try_reduce_nat itself to reduce an expression still marked as having free variables. The local guard always returns None. The mode-sensitive outer guard can allow native reduction of a closed side while the other side remains open. A pair consisting only of free-variable Nat operations cannot establish the requested distinction merely by toggling the mode.

For expressions still closed at these direct guards, the disjunct involving eager_mode cannot change guard eligibility. This does not prove global mode equivalence: comparisons of binders may introduce locals or nested inference may set eager mode.

The Bool shortcut evaluates the lhs earlier with full WHNF; lazy delta has other paths to unfold definitions and establish equality. Different evaluation order alone does not establish a pair with distinct returned Booleans or a Lean semantic discrepancy. Neither global equivalence nor a soundness bug is established by this review.

Positive eq_cache is unordered and mode-independent and consulted before negative lookup. Any success reaching the final result block warms it, so a subsequent lazy call can return true regardless of its cold behavior. The Bool fast-return itself does not insert a positive entry. Future cells must document which success path occurred and use separate fresh-control contexts plus a same-context negative-then-eager sequence; clearing all caches between stages would fail to exercise negative-cache isolation.

congr_fail_cache is a different unordered mode-independent cache. Its hit skips a congruence shortcut and allows unfolding; it is not a direct global def_eq=false cache. WHNF and inference caches also survive within the same checker. Record them or justify why they cannot explain a staged observation.

Checked application inference temporarily enables eager mode when its argument is syntactically a two-argument application of the cached eagerReduce name, then checks binder_type against arg_type in that order and restores the old mode after success. Direct test mutation of the internal flag would scope the test to the internal API, not demonstrate public importer reachability.

Prior same-TypeChecker helper construction and direct internal-cache assertions are reusable patterns. The existing malformed-let pair tests InferOnly/Check separation and uses sort comparisons that exit def_eq_quick_check; it is not an eager-mode negative-cache witness. The retained patch is historical evidence; do not modify it or mechanically assume its text is a clean current patch.

independent_assessment.outcome: BOUNDED_UNRESOLVED for a mode-differentiating same-context outcome sequence; useful exact source exclusions and test inventory established.
independent_assessment.remaining_route: Need a fully specified type-correct open/closed comparison or Bool eager-shortcut example whose ordinary path returns false and eager path true, with the ordinary call reaching negative-cache insertion and no warmed positive explaining the second result. This review does not exhibit such a sequence.
independent_assessment.alternative_test_value: A lifecycle/order/key-membership test with mode-invariant false results could prevent accidental changes to the declared cache representation and clear behavior, but cannot demonstrate why the mode bit is semantically necessary. Adding it solely to mirror the field type has lower expected ecosystem value than the independently READY Arena reserve. Do not manufacture a claimed behavioral regression from fabricated cache entries.
